answer.evidence: The object is a 160x112 floor terrain tile, not a standing object. The width profile is a constant 160 for rows 0-111, so there is no silhouette change, no ellipse, and no front-edge line. Rows 0-2 at the top and the left columns hold a dark contact shadow beneath the wall, as the name describes. The rest is a light-blue ice texture of patches, cracks and highlights with no vertical front face. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is an ice floor with several light-to-mid blue steps (about 5): white highlights, pale ice, mid blue patches and darker blue crack lines. It has real texture: dither-like hatching in the patches, speckled white frost, and carved crack lines. Flat-fill coverage is 1%, in line with the references' 0%. It has 36 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile. That matches the paving reference (7) but is below the grass reference (26), so density is slightly lower than the richest reference. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so they carry a tint. The only dark edge is the soft contact shadow under the wall at the top and left, which is a tinted blue-grey and not a sticker outline. The patch has no outline around shapes, and forms are separated by value, which suits a floor. A careful artist would accept it next to the references; it is not flatter or thinner than the paving, and the texture is varied.
